title: Xbox Series LB RB repair

tools.text: A small knife or utility blade with a sharp edge.
A rounded tip or soft tool for scraping the metal.

introduction_raw:
[video|https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4-W55VYxxsY]

If the ***LB or RB button on your Xbox controller isn't responding*** or you have to press it very hard, the problem is usually ***dirt accumulated inside***.

In this guide, we show you step by step with photos how to ***open the button, clean it, and get it working*** again.
conclusion_raw: The LB/RB failure described here is almost always caused by carbon buildup on the microswitch contacts, not by a failed component — which makes this a cleaning and reseating job rather than a parts-replacement repair. The 16 steps walk through opening the switch, scraping and polishing the dome and contact pads, and sealing the housing back up with epoxy.

lines.text_raw: We connect the controller to confirm that the ***LB or RB button doesn't respond*** or fails when pressed.
With the knife held flat, we very carefully cut the tips of the plastic posts holding the ***metal cap***.
Rest your fingers firmly on the green board to control the force and avoid cutting yourself.
We remove all the leftover plastic so the ***metal cap is free*** of any obstruction.
Be careful not to scrape the ***green coating of the logic board*** with the knife edge.
We insert the tip of the knife under the edge and lift the ***metal cover*** very gently.
Keep the cap in a safe place on your mat so it doesn't get lost.
We remove the small ***black plastic center piece*** using the fine tweezers.
We turn the board face-down so the ***curved metal plate*** falls out on its own onto the table without bending.
At the bottom of the button you'll see ***dark stains like ash or soot*** on the three terminals.
That black dirt builds up with every click and prevents the console from receiving your command.
With the tip of the tweezers we very slowly scrape the ***center circle and the two edges***.
Don't dig the tip in with force—just rub it gently until the metal shines again.
We moisten a small cotton ball with ***isopropyl alcohol***.
We clean the inside of the button to remove all the loose black dust.
If you look at the plate from the side, you'll notice it has a ***small rounded curve***.
That shape is what makes the click when you play, so never flatten or deform it.
We hold the plate with the tweezers barely touching the edges so we don't flatten it.
With a ***smooth rounded tip*** we gently rub its underside to remove all the burnt soot.
We pass another small piece of cotton with alcohol to clean the plate completely.
You'll see the cotton come out stained black and the ***metal left shiny***.
The ***shiny, domed side*** must face up, toward where you're looking at it.
The side we scraped and polished should face down toward the bottom of the button.
We place the ***small black plastic button*** right in the middle of the metal plate.
We put the metal cap on top and press with the tweezers so it seats in place.
Since we cut the factory posts, we now need to ***seal the structure*** so it doesn't come apart.
We mix equal parts of the two glue tubes until it's an even gray color.
We spread a little ***epoxy glue on the metal corners*** and on the plastic sides.
***Never touch the black button in the center*** with glue or it will be stuck forever.
We let the glue dry for about 10 minutes before reassembling the controller shells.
Test the controller on the console and you'll notice the ***button clicks softly again and responds on the first press***.
